overview: Natural Language Processing (NLP) is the multidisciplinary field focused on the interaction between computers and human language. It combines linguistics, computer science, and machine learning to enable machines to understand, interpret, and generate text.
From simple sentiment analysis to complex LLMs like GPT-4, NLP is the technology behind the conversational interfaces and translation tools we use every day.

topics.title: Text Preprocessing & Tokenization
theory: Before a computer can process text, it must be broken down into smaller units called 'tokens'. Tokenizers can operate at the word level, character level, or sub-word level (like BPE used in modern LLMs).
Preprocessing also involves 'Normalization'—removing stop words (common words like 'the' or 'is'), lowercasing, and 'Lemmatization' (reducing words to their base dictionary form).
visualIntuition: Think of a sentence as a Lego castle. Tokenization is the process of breaking the castle down into its individual bricks so you can count them, categorize them, and store them in buckets.

topics.title: Word Embeddings (Word2Vec & GloVe)
theory: Computers cannot understand raw words; they need numbers. Word embeddings are a way of representing words as dense vectors in high-dimensional space.
In this vector space, words with similar meanings (like 'king' and 'queen') are placed close together. This allows models to capture semantic relationships: 'King - Man + Woman ≈ Queen'.
visualIntuition: Imagine a massive map where every word is a city. Cities that produce similar goods (have similar meanings) are built near each other. You can calculate the distance between 'Apple' and 'Fruit' to see how related they are.
visualSuggestions: 3D scatter plot showing clusters of related words (e.g., animals, sports, technology).
Interactive vector math demonstration showing the 'King-Man+Woman' relationship.

topics.title: The Transformer Architecture
theory: Transformers revolutionized NLP by introducing 'Attention'. Unlike older models (RNNs) that read text sequentially from left to right, Transformers look at the entire sentence at once.

The 'Self-Attention' mechanism allows the model to determine which words are most relevant to each other, regardless of their distance. For example, in 'The bank of the river', attention helps the model know that 'bank' refers to land, not money.
visualIntuition: Imagine you are in a crowded room. Even though everyone is talking, you 'attend' to the one person speaking your name. Transformers do this for every word in a sentence simultaneously.
visualSuggestions: Attention mask visualization showing links between related words in a sentence.
Comparison of Sequential (RNN) vs Parallel (Transformer) processing flow.

code.content:
import numpy as np

def softmax(x):
    e_x = np.exp(x - np.max(x))
    return e_x / e_x.sum(axis=-1)

# Query, Key, Value vectors for 3 words
Q = np.array([[1, 0, 1], [0, 1, 0], [1, 1, 0]])
K = np.array([[1, 0, 1], [0, 1, 0], [1, 1, 0]])

scores = Q @ K.T
weights = softmax(scores)
print("Attention Weights:\n", weights)
